sharedContract.problem: Clip coverage correctly ignored child strokes, but resource bounds also discarded them. Native clip construction uses the child visual enclosure, including stroke presentation even when its paint server is unavailable. A smaller enclosure changes curve construction before painting or blurring.
sharedContract.change: Direct, primitive, inherited, union and referenced clip producers preserve visual bounds separately from the silhouette. SvgStrokeStyleSyntax.BoundsInflation shares the existing native calculation with ordinary paint recording, with cap eligibility limited to paths/point lists/lines. SvgClipPolygon.ResourceBounds carries the result; existing clip construction consumes it.
sharedContract.referencedSources: SvgDefinitionLeafSource.LowerClip reuses ordinary leaf lowerers with opaque fill and ignored paint/stroke/effects. It preserves authored operands and computes visual stroke inflation from cascaded style separately. Visibility applies after geometry admission, keeping hidden-source and single-contour contracts. No stroke paint server is required for silhouette construction.
sharedContract.ownership: No new owner, cache, bitmap kind or public API. Pending rectangles retain one extra scalar beside existing placement until a sibling requires native replay. Cascaded presentation strings use the existing document store. Temporary referenced geometry is released before adoption of its mapped copy; failure, cancellation and retry retain existing cleanup.
sharedContract.containment: Visual union bounds include every authored child even when one rectangle contains another silhouette. The normalized rectangle clip uses its retained geometry, never the visual enclosure. Two focused regressions fail against the intermediate model and pass after separating these roles.

nativeSources.contract: CalculateLocalClipBounds maps each contributing child VisualRectInLocalSVGCoordinates. CalculateStrokeBoundingBox uses the approximate native stroke enclosure; clip-path coverage ignores stroke paint.
